facts.statement: The only known fossil of Paraphysornis is a nearly complete skeleton discovered between 1977 and 1978.
facts.quote: It is known from a single, nearly complete skeleton that was unearthed between 1977 and 1978.

facts.statement: Paraphysornis lived around 23 million years ago during the Late Oligocene to Early Miocene in what is now southern Brazil.
facts.quote: It lived during the Late Oligocene to Early Miocene (around 23 million years ago) in what is now southern Brazil.

facts.statement: Excavation yielded a 75% complete skeleton that lacked most of the cranium, pelvis, and sternum.
facts.quote: Excavation of the bones took several months between 1977 and 1978, yielding a nearly complete (75%) skeleton, only lacking most of the cranium, the pelvis and sternum.

facts.statement: The genus name Paraphysornis combines the name Physornis with the Greek suffix "para-" to mean "close to Physornis".
facts.quote: The name is a combination of the genus name of Physornis and the Greek suffix "para-", in combination meaning "close to Physornis".

facts.statement: Few cranial elements are preserved, including quadrates and a premaxilla with a strongly hooked tip similar to other phorusrhacids.
facts.quote: Only few elements of the cranium are preserved including the quadrates and their articulation with the mandible as well as the front of the premaxilla, which shows a strongly hooked tip as known from other phorusrhacids.

facts.statement: The preserved vertebral column includes thirteen cervical vertebrae arranged in an S-curve with strong curvature in the upper section and less curvature in the lower section.
facts.quote: The vertebral column is well preserved and shows the presence of thirteen cervical vertebrae displaying strong curvature (kyphosis) over cervicals one to five and a less developed curvature (lordosis) over cervicals eight to twelve, with those between these sections articulating almost straight, which gives the animal's neck the traditional avian S-curve.

facts.statement: Nearly the entire left wing and some right wing elements are preserved, showing wings heavily reduced even more than in other phorusrhacids.
facts.quote: Almost the entire left wing is preserved with some elements also being present on the right side of the skeleton. Like in other flightless birds, the wings are heavily reduced, evenmore so than in other phorusrhacids.

facts.statement: Unlike other phorusrhacids, Paraphysornis lacks preserved quill knobs, suggesting its feathers were not as strongly anchored.
facts.quote: Unlike other phorusrhacids, Paraphysornis preserves no indication of quill knobs, attachment points for strong pennacious feathers.

facts.statement: The femur is missing its shaft, but estimates based on Brontornis proportions suggest a length of 35 cm.
facts.quote: The femur preserves both the proximal and distal ends but is missing the shaft, making it impossible to determine the exact length of the bone. However, estimates based on the proportions of Brontornis might indicate a length of 35 cm.

facts.statement: The tarsometatarsus is notably short, measuring only half the length of the long, robust tibiotarsus.
facts.quote: The tibiotarsus is long, straight and robust, while the tarsometatarsus is notably short, only half the length of the tibiotarsus.

facts.statement: The mandible anatomy and claw shape indicate that Paraphysornis was a carnivore like other phorusrhacids.
facts.quote: The anatomy of the mandible and the shape of the claws both clearly suggest that the bird was a carnivore, like other Phorusrhacids.

facts.statement: Unable to chase fast prey, Paraphysornis likely hunted using ambush tactics or scavenging.
facts.quote: Due to not being able to chase fast-running prey, it may have had a specific hunting method (ambush, scavenger).

facts.statement: Paraphysornis lived in the Tremembé Formation, which preserves evidence of a shallow lake environment.
facts.quote: Paraphysornis lived during the Late Oligocene or Early Miocene in the Tremembé Formation, which preserves what is thought to be a shallow lake.

facts.statement: Paraphysornis is traditionally classified in the subfamily Brontornithinae alongside Brontornis and Physornis.
facts.quote: Due to these shared features, Paraphysornis is traditionally considered a member of Brontornithinae alongside Brontornis and Physornis.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Brontornis is a true phorusrhacid or a gastornithiform anserimorph, which affects the classification of related genera.
facts.quote: However, the nature of this clade has come into question, with some researchers arguing that Brontornis does in fact not represent a phorusrhacid and may instead be a gastornithiform anserimorph.

facts.statement: Agnolin proposed the subfamily name Physornithinae for a clade containing Physornis and Paraphysornis.
facts.quote: Although the matter is debated, Agnolin proposed the name Physornithinae for a clade containing both Physornis and Paraphysornis.

facts.statement: The time range for Paraphysornis is estimated from 27.3 to 23.04 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Chattian to Chattian (27.3 to 23.04 million years ago)

facts.statement: The humerus is heavily curved with an almost elliptical shaft.
facts.quote: The humerus is heavily curved and its shaft almost elliptical in shape.

facts.statement: The ulna is well preserved and notably more atrophied than that of Mesembriornis.
facts.quote: The ulna is preserved in excellent condition and notably more atrophied than in Mesembriornis.

facts.statement: The anterior and superior portions of the pelvis are preserved, showing an iliac crest similar to Psilopterus and Mesembriornis.
facts.quote: The pelvis is too poorly preserved to give an idea of its morphology, however its anterior and superior portions are present and preserve the iliac crest, which appears similar to that of Psilopterus and Mesembriornis.

rejected.quote: The holotype (DGM-1418-R) and only known fossil was discovered by a mining company in the Taubaté Basin (São Paulo State) in a layer of bentonite clay, two or three meters below a layer of Pyrobitumen.
